result.summary:
Reviewed the full REQ-038 diff (git diff master...HEAD, 22 files, +1876/-85) against docs/agents/design/REQ-038.md line by line, plus docs/agents/anti-patterns.md and reviewer.md's apps/bot-specific rules. Findings below; no gaps found, PASS granted.

1. hasPastCheckIn integration (design §2.2): confirmed in apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts -- a single new line `const inviteSatisfied = event.requiresInvite ? await hasPastCheckIn(tx, userId) : false;` is inserted between the existing locked event read and the existing decideRegistrationOutcome call, using the already-open `tx` handle. registerForEvent's exported signature is textually unchanged (db, userId, eventId, evaluationTime); handlers/registration.ts's register:<eventId> callback call site has zero diff and needed no edit -- confirmed by re-reading that call site directly, not from the handoff's claim alone.

2. Distinct refusal wording: read apps/bot/src/i18n/en.ts and ru.ts directly. refusedInviteCodeNotFound ('That invite code isn't recognized.') and refusedInviteCodeNotYours ('That invite code was issued to someone else.') are genuinely different strings in both languages -- confirmed, matching design §3.2's identity-leakage reasoning (>=128-bit code entropy makes the distinct message safe to show).

3. Atomic used_count increment: apps/bot/src/domain/inviteCode.ts's redeemInviteCode locks invite_codes FOR UPDATE at step 5 (fresh read, never reusing the unlocked precheck), and the increment (`usedCount: codeRow.usedCount + 1`) happens only inside the branch reached after a writing outcome (admitted/waitlisted/requested), in the same db.transaction callback as the registrations INSERT/UPDATE and the writeAuditLog call. Non-writing outcomes (step 9) return before that point -- used_count is provably untouched on any refusal or non-writing outcome.

4. Consent-gate reuse: traced handlers/start.ts's resolveInviteDeepLink -- checks !hasConsented first, sends the same buildConsentKeyboard(lang, payloadText) the event branch uses, returns before any DB read of invite_codes/registrations. makeConsentCallbackHandler gains one new `else if (payload.kind === "invite")` sibling branch, same position, same `true` (already-consented) argument, calling resolveInviteDeepLink -- identical shape to the existing event branch, no divergence.

5. decideRegistrationOutcome diff: confirmed minimal -- one new field on RegistrationDecisionInput (inviteSatisfied: boolean), and the requires-invite branch changed from `if (input.requiresInvite)` to `if (input.requiresInvite && !input.inviteSatisfied)`. Every other line/branch of the function is untouched (confirmed via the diff, not the design doc's claim). The REQ-020 placeholder ('requires-invite' with no onward path) is genuinely replaced -- handlers/registrationReply.ts's composeRegistrationReply now returns refusedRequiresInvite + refusedRequiresInviteHint + deepLinkSeeUpcoming for that case; no dead placeholder branch left alongside it.

6. registrationReply.ts (new file): read in full. It is composeRegistrationReply and resolveRegistrationOutcomeDisplayData moved verbatim (non-invite-code cases byte-for-byte identical to the prior handlers/registration.ts private function) out to a third module so both handlers/registration.ts and handlers/start.ts can import it without a start.ts<->registration.ts cycle -- neither file imports the other, both import only registrationReply.ts. This is plumbing, not a new architectural decision; STATUS_CATALOG_KEY is re-exported from registration.ts unchanged so handlers/my.ts's existing import keeps working with zero edit there. No behavior change, no scope creep.

7. registration.test.ts's edit: one line, `inviteSatisfied: false` added to the baseInput fixture's default overrides object -- required because RegistrationDecisionInput gained a mandatory new field; every existing test's assertions are otherwise untouched (confirmed by the diff showing exactly one line changed). Not a weakened assertion.

8. No schema/migration/Wishlist/second-generator: git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts is empty (zero lines). No file under any migrations directory changed. grep -ril wishlist across apps/bot only hits pre-existing, untouched files (organizerRequests.ts, registrationApproval.db.test.ts, and their dist/ build artifacts) -- confirmed these are not part of this diff via git diff master...HEAD --name-only.

9. No npm workspace added/renamed/removed, no build-output relocation -- Dockerfile re-verification (reviewer.md item 7) is not triggered; skipped correctly.

10. apps/bot decision-record checks: all new domain logic (validateInviteCodeForRedemption, redeemInviteCode, hasPastCheckIn, decideRegistrationOutcome's new term) lives in apps/bot/src/domain/{inviteCode,registration}.ts, framework-free -- no grammY import in either file (confirmed by the import lists in the diff). Handlers (registration.ts, start.ts, registrationReply.ts) only call the domain functions and compose replies -- no admission-state rule written inside a handler body. grep for now()/current_timestamp in inviteCode.ts and registration.ts finds none used inside a predicate -- evaluationTime is an explicit parameter throughout, matching decisions/0006.

Verification re-run independently (real output, this REVIEWER pass): `npm run lint -w apps/bot` -- clean, zero errors/warnings. `npm run build -w apps/bot` -- clean tsc build, zero errors. `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -- 42/42 test files, 384/384 tests passed, single clean run, no ISS-0031 contention pattern, no rerun needed.

Scope: the diff does exactly what REQ-038 asks (i_ deep link + /redeem command, the five-case validation table, past-check-in eligibility, atomic used_count increment, consent-gate preservation, distinct refusal copy) and nothing more -- the three open questions the design itself flagged (companion-code host-linking, /redeem's raw-UUID-only event id, no rate-limiting) are correctly left unresolved rather than silently decided in code.
